description: A software release, judged: should you give a shit about this upgrade? YAML frontmatter built key by key, a TL;DR callout, breaking changes behind a danger callout, highlights with vendor claims quoted and deep-linked into the changelog, an upgrade-math table, an upgrade-path section with a task-list preflight, numbered steps, a sh code block and a folded rollback callout, known issues, an embedded migration guide, wikilinked receipts and footnotes. Section headings, callout kinds and callout titles belong to the template; write values only. The template does all layout; strings hold text, not markup — except that `voice: true` fields may carry constrained inline formatting (**, *, ~~ on words the reply added, code spans quoting the input, allowlisted emoji within the tone's budget).

product.role: product name; frontmatter `product`, and the page heading when `title` is absent

version.role: version string, rendered as inline code, e.g. 2.0.0

title.role: page heading; falls back to `product` via ??. Its kebab-case form becomes frontmatter `slug`, so it is never rewritten

codename.role: release codename, frontmatter only; falls back to a stock line via ??

date.role: release date, YYYY-MM-DD; frontmatter `released` and the meta line

verdict.role: two-to-four word upgrade verdict, rendered bold, e.g. upgrade now|wait for .1|skip it

take.role: one-line hot take after the verdict

related.role: names of existing site pages; rendered as [[wikilinks]] in frontmatter `related` and in the 'Filed under' link cloud. Name only pages that exist; an invented name is a dangling wikilink

screenshot_alt.role: alt text for `screenshot`; falls back to `product`

tldr.role: 2-4 sentence summary, single paragraph, body of the 'TL;DR' tip callout

breaking_warning.role: body of the 'Read this before you upgrade' danger callout; falls back to a stock warning via ??. Only shown when `breaking` is non-empty

change.role: what broke, one line, h3 heading

fix.role: what to do about it, 1-3 sentences

note.role: key into `notes`; renders a [^key] footnote ref. Must match a `notes` key exactly

highlights.role: what actually changed, one h3 each

name.role: feature name, one line, h3 heading

what.role: what it does and why you care, 1-3 sentences

claim.role: the vendor's own words, copied verbatim from the page at `changelog_url`, one line. Rendered in a 'Their words, not ours' quote callout with a #:~:text= deep link, so it must match the changelog text exactly

note.role: key into `notes`; renders a [^key] footnote ref

upgrade_matrix.role: rows of the 'Upgrade math' pipe table, one per starting version; the header (you are on | effort | downtime | should you bother) is fixed in the template. `on` is the starting version, `effort` the work, `downtime` the outage, `bother` the recommendation. No | or newlines in values

preflight.role: pre-upgrade checks, one task-list item each, imperative, under 12 words. Rendered as a `- [ ]` checklist under 'Before you start'

upgrade_steps.role: the upgrade procedure in order, one numbered step each, imperative, one line. Put the command in `upgrade_command`, not here

upgrade_command.role: the one shell command that performs the upgrade, copied verbatim from the release notes or upgrade docs. Rendered as a ```sh code block. One line, never contains a backtick fence

rollback.role: rollback procedure in order, one numbered step each. Rendered inside a collapsed 'Rollback plan' warning callout

known_issues.role: what is still broken, one bullet each

migration_guide.role: name of an existing site page, embedded as ![[name]]

changelog_url.role: release notes or changelog URL (http/https, no #fragment); the 'Full changelog' link and the deep-link target for every highlight `claim`

notes.role: footnotes: key -> note text, rendered as [^key]: definitions. Keys are short kebab-case labels. Every key must be referenced by some `note`, and every `note` must be a key here; format_check flags strays. As a ratchet step the server picks the key and the item it attaches to; write the note text only, copied verbatim from a source
